user_consequence: A player mid-round-entry (or any dirty form) on a flaky mobile connection can have the ENTIRE document silently replaced (window.location.replace) with zero check for unsaved/local work, and this can recur repeatedly across a session rather than being capped once — because the very success of the recovery (a fresh hydrated mount) re-arms the budget that was supposed to cap it.
mechanism: Four independent global error-listening mechanisms are mounted unconditionally in the root layout (src/app/layout.tsx:138,148,149 — StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript, ChunkLoadErrorHandler, GlobalErrorHandlerSetup — plus RouteErrorBoundary wherever a route error.tsx uses it) and none is aware of the others. (1) StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript.tsx's beforeInteractive inline script installs window 'error'/'unhandledrejection' listeners (lines 152-177) whose isStaleDeploymentError (lines 30-46) matches the BARE generic string `lower === 'load failed'` (the common iOS WebKit fetch-failure message) as well as 'an unexpected response was received from the server' and chunk-load/server-action phrases — any match calls reloadFresh() (lines 115-150), which clears caches/service workers then does `window.location.replace` with NO check for a dirty form, an in-progress round, or any other unsaved state. Its only safeguard is MAX_RELOADS=3 read from a URL query param (`__deployment_refresh`) plus a 12s cooldown read from sessionStorage key `chunk-error-reload`. (2) ChunkLoadErrorHandler.tsx mounts as a React effect (line 13-25) that runs on every successful client mount/hydration and UNCONDITIONALLY strips the `__deployment_refresh` URL param (line 16-18) and removes the `chunk-error-reload` sessionStorage key (line 24) — i.e. every successful page load resets the reload budget and cooldown to zero, regardless of how many reloads happened earlier in the session. So a user hitting the generic 'Load failed' error once per navigation (plausible on an unreliable mobile network, since this string is the default WebKit fetch-abort message) can be reloaded up to 3 times, land safely, have the counter cleared, then get reloaded up to 3 more times on the next failure, indefinitely across a session. (3) RouteErrorBoundary.tsx (a separate Next.js error.tsx boundary) independently reuses the SAME `chunk-error-reload` sessionStorage key (lines 152-159) but with different semantics (presence/absence flag rather than a timestamp+URL-count budget) to gate its own `window.location.reload()` for a real ChunkLoadError, and ALSO auto-retries (lines 229-263) generic 'load failed'/'failed to fetch' errors via `reset()` on a separate per-route sessionStorage budget (`route-auto-retry:${route}`). (4) src/lib/error-logging.ts's setupGlobalErrorHandlers (lines 630-679, mounted via GlobalErrorHandlerSetup.tsx at layout.tsx:149) registers a SECOND, entirely separate pair of window 'error'/'unhandledrejection' listeners that independently detect 'was not found on the server'/stale-server-action messages and call softReloadForStaleServerAction() (lines 527-576), which does its own toast + `window.location.reload()` gated on a THIRD sessionStorage key (`stale-action-auto-reload`) and a module-level flag. A single stale-server-action error message matches BOTH mechanism (1)'s isStaleDeploymentError classifier (script's line 38-39: `lower.includes('server action') && ...'was not found'`) and mechanism (4)'s isStaleServerActionError — so both fire independently for the same event, racing two uncoordinated reload attempts.
expected: Per plan §9.1/T01/T02/C09: one bounded recovery coordinator; a session/release recovery budget that survives a successful mount; no automatic document reload while a dirty form/active operation exists.
actual: Four uncoordinated reload paths, three different sessionStorage keys with inconsistent semantics, a reload budget that resets to zero on every successful hydration (the opposite of 'survives a successful mount'), and zero unsaved-work guard anywhere in the chain before window.location.replace/reload fires.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL (not authored here — coordinator decision): consolidate to one C09 recovery coordinator module owning classification, a SINGLE session-scoped (not per-mount-cleared) attempt ledger, and a hook the round-entry/dirty-form owners can register an 'unsaved work' guard against before any reload is allowed to fire. Do not add a fifth mechanism; retire the redundant three.
owner_lane: A02 (shell/recovery contract); A05 coordinates the round-entry dirty-work guard; A01 coordinates native cache/service-worker cooperation.
accessibility_check: NOT_RUN — no screen-reader announcement exists for an in-flight recovery reload; a VoiceOver user gets no warning before the document is replaced.
performance_check: NOT_RUN — no device to measure actual reload frequency under real network flakiness.

user_consequence: While a bottom-tab navigation is in flight, the tapped tab's icon and label visibly shift position (not just gain a new element) because the pending indicator is a real layout participant, not an overlay — contradicting the plan's own pending-geometry gate (Section 11.2: 'no unintended icon/label/container displacement').
mechanism: NavPendingDot (src/components/fairway/app-shell/NavPending.tsx:56-79) renders `null` when idle (no layout cost) but, when `useLinkStatus().pending` is true, renders an in-flow `<span>` (a 6px dot) as the THIRD child inside FairwayBottomNav.tsx's per-tab `<Link>`, whose container is `flex min-h-[56px] flex-col items-center justify-center` (FairwayBottomNav.tsx:193) — i.e. icon-span, label-span, then conditionally the dot-span, all vertically centered as one flex column. Adding the dot increases the column's total content height by ~8px (dot + `mt-0.5` margin, FairwayBottomNav.tsx:231), so `justify-center` re-centers the taller three-item stack, moving the icon and label upward within the fixed 56px-tall tab for the duration of the pending navigation, then back down on arrival — a real, measurable displacement, not merely 'additive' as the component's own header comment claims (NavPending.tsx:31-34).
expected: Plan §11.2: 'No unintended icon/label/container displacement; allow at most 1 CSS-pixel measurement tolerance for rounding, not a design shift.'
actual: A conditionally-rendered in-flow sibling changes the flex column's content height, re-centering icon+label under `justify-center` for the pending duration.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: reserve the dot's space unconditionally (render it always, toggle only opacity/visibility) so the column's content height — and therefore the `justify-center` midpoint — never changes between idle and pending, matching the reserved-slot pattern the plan requires elsewhere (§8.3 'Reserve icon/spinner slots so label and bounds do not shift when busy').

user_consequence: Opening a drill/detail view inside a stage (e.g. a CoachHelm Player Home Bento cell, or a Stats spine drill) and then pressing the native platform Back button does not return the user to the stage's home/list view — because no history entry was ever created for that 'deeper destination', Back instead leaves the page entirely (to whatever the browser/native history had before the page load). Separately, every stage swap forcibly scrolls the viewport to bring the new stage view into focus, even when returning 'home' from a scrolled-down position.
mechanism: StageRouter.tsx's `open()` (lines 143-156) always routes through `replaceStageUrl()` (lines 47-76), which unconditionally calls `window.history.replaceState` (line 68) for every stage-key change — there is no branch that pushes a history entry for a 'deeper destination' (opening a drill) versus replacing for a 'reversible same-level mode' (switching between sibling tabs), despite the plan's own Section 9.3 explicitly requiring that distinction ('Use detail push/history or an explicit back stack for a deeper destination; use replace for filters and reversible same-level modes'). Separately, every non-initial stage swap (StageRouter.tsx:135-141) calls `stageViewRef.current?.focus({preventScroll: false})` unconditionally — `preventScroll: false` permits the browser's default scroll-into-view behavior, and there is no check for whether the stage container is already within the visible viewport before allowing that scroll, so a stage swap from a scrolled position can silently reposition the page. The view also fully remounts on every swap via `key={activeView.key}` (line 169), discarding any DOM/scroll state inside the previous view unconditionally, which is deliberate for the entrance-fade replay but compounds the 'no local drill history' problem: a user drilled two levels deep and pressing Back cannot use in-page state to reconstruct where they were.
expected: Plan §9.3 and the A02 work order bullet: 'Define detail push, filter replace, local drill history, native Back, external-entry fallback, return anchor and same-tab repeat behavior. Stage replacement and focus({preventScroll:false}) require deliberate testing, not blanket conversion of all replaces to pushes.'
actual: Every stage change — regardless of whether it is conceptually a 'deeper destination' or a 'same-level mode' — uses replace-only history, and every swap unconditionally permits scroll-into-view on focus.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL (product/architecture decision, not authored here — this is exactly what G18 flags as needing one): classify each StageRouter consumer's views as home/sibling (replace, current behavior is correct) vs. drill/detail (push, or an explicit in-memory back stack scoped to the stage) so native Back exits a drill to its stage's home rather than off the page; and gate the focus-driven scroll on actual viewport intersection (only scroll if the stage container is not already visible), consistent with Section 9.3's 'Only scroll the active field when actually obscured.'
owner_lane: A02 (owns StageRouter per the plan's chokepoint table); A06 (Stats spine drills) and CoachHelm player-home consumers apply the resulting contract.
accessibility_check: The focus-management intent (moving focus into the new stage view for keyboard/AT users) is itself correct and should be preserved — only the unconditional scroll permission needs gating.
performance_check: NOT_RUN — requires a mounted browser to observe actual scroll-jump behavior.

mechanism: `src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/template.tsx` is a Next.js `template.tsx` file, which by the framework's own contract creates a NEW component instance of its children on every navigation to a route nested under it (unlike `layout.tsx`, which persists) — this file wraps the entire golf dashboard content tree (every page under `/golf/dashboard/*`) in exactly that boundary. user_consequence: Leaving Home/Stats/Rounds and coming back to any of them (e.g. Home -> Stats -> Home) shows the FULL page skeleton again rather than the previously-loaded, still-valid content with a quiet local refresh — even though the underlying data has not become stale in any way the user would recognize as needing a full reload.
mechanism: `src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:28`, `stats/page.tsx:15`, and `rounds/page.tsx:22` each declare `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`. Next.js's App Router client-side Router Cache defaults dynamic segments to a 0-second stale time (only static segments default to ~5 minutes) unless `experimental.staleTimes` is configured to override it; `next.config.*` (checked lines ~165-230, the whole `experimental` block) declares no `staleTimes` override. Combined with every one of these routes shipping its own `loading.tsx` (confirmed present for `dashboard/`, `dashboard/stats/`, `dashboard/rounds/`, and in fact essentially every dashboard sub-route — 40+ `loading.tsx` files under `src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/`), and combined with A02-004's template.tsx remount making every navigation a fresh instance, a return-navigation to any of these force-dynamic routes re-fetches the RSC payload from zero and re-renders that route's full-page `loading.tsx` skeleton, exactly the 'same-scope background refresh' scenario Section 9.1/T05 forbids from becoming a full-page skeleton.
expected: Plan §9.1: 'Usable data, same-scope refresh -> Existing content with quiet local progress only if useful. Preserve: Component identity, scroll, selection, input.' §11.2: 'Same-scope refresh -> Zero full-page/full-list replacement while usable authorized data exists.'
actual: Zero client-side cache retention for these force-dynamic routes (default Next.js behavior, unmodified by this repo's config), so every return-navigation is architecturally guaranteed to show the full-route `loading.tsx` skeleton again, not the prior content.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: this is the C02 scoped-read contract's core job — either configure `experimental.staleTimes.dynamic` to a small nonzero window (a global, coarse fix) and/or give the highest-traffic routes (Home, Stats, Rounds) a client-side data cache keyed by scope (team/date/filter) so a same-scope return shows the last good render immediately with a quiet background revalidation, per C02's 'availability, freshness ... revision and result scope' fields. A global `staleTimes` change affects every dynamic route in the app (not just golf) and needs A00 sign-off; a per-route client cache is the narrower, safer first step.
owner_lane: A02 (shell/C02 pattern); A04 (Home), A06 (Stats) own applying it to their page data-fetch boundaries.
performance_check: NOT_RUN — needs A11 to measure actual navigation-timing deltas; the architectural cause (zero cache retention) is source-certain.

confidence: low (no current collision exists; this is a latent-fragility risk, not an active defect)
user_consequence: If a future StageRouter instance is ever added reusing an existing `param` name (`view` or `area`) on a page that also mounts an existing StageRouter, opening a stage in one would silently navigate the other, since the sync mechanism is a single, unscoped, page-global event.
mechanism: StageRouter's cross-instance sync uses a bare `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('helm:stage-navigation', {detail: {param, key}}))` (StageRouter.tsx:70-74) filtered only by `detail.param !== param` (StageRouter.tsx:120) — there is no per-instance identity (no id, no DOM scoping), so any two StageRouter instances mounted simultaneously with the same `param` string would cross-fire. Today's two production mounts use different params (`PlayerCoachHelmHome.tsx:421` uses `param="view"`; `StatsSpineStage.tsx:599` uses `param="area"`), so no active collision exists at this baseline.
expected: A shared cross-instance sync mechanism should not be able to cross-fire two independent instances that happen to share a param name.
actual: No instance scoping exists; correctness currently depends entirely on every future caller picking a distinct `param` string, which is convention, not enforcement.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: add a lightweight per-mount instance id to the event detail (or scope the listener to a DOM ancestor) so a future param collision fails safely instead of silently cross-navigating.

user_consequence: Under a scenario where GlobalErrorHandlerSetup's effect runs more than once in a session (React StrictMode double-invoke in dev, or any future remount of this component), duplicate 'error'/'unhandledrejection' listeners would stack, each independently classifying and logging/reloading for the same event.
mechanism: `setupGlobalErrorHandlers()` (error-logging.ts:630) unconditionally calls `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ...)` and `window.addEventListener('error', ...)` with no re-entrancy guard, unlike StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript's own inline script which explicitly guards itself with `window.__helmv3StaleDeploymentRecoveryInstalled` (StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript.tsx:5-6) specifically to prevent double-installation. `GlobalErrorHandlerSetup.tsx`'s `useEffect(() => { setupGlobalErrorHandlers(); }, [])` (lines 11-13) has no cleanup/removeEventListener and no external guard either, relying entirely on the component mounting exactly once for the life of the tab (true today, per layout.tsx:149's single mount) — but nothing enforces that invariant if the component is ever moved or remounted.
expected: A global listener installer should be idempotent, matching the pattern its sibling mechanism (StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript) already uses.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: add the same kind of one-time-install guard (a module-level boolean or a `window.__` flag) that StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript already uses, so this stays safe regardless of future mount changes.
